title: Nuclear shell closure, g-block filling and the predicted periodic endpoint
description:
Read the full mathematical paper (PDF)

Smithium: Z = 126, N = 184, A = 310, with active electronic configuration 8s²5g⁶. The generated g-block opens at 121 and the exact structural periodic endpoint is 137.

Maria Smith derives the nuclear sequence 2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126, 184 from complete three-direction compositions, two Fold labels and the first whole-gap action of the exact colour coupling 2/3. The all-rank successor law proves that 126 is the next closure after 82 and 184 the next after 126.

The independent orbital law 2[1+2(r−1)] gives capacities 2, 6, 10, 14, 18. A complete joint-cover ordering generates the electronic walk through the 118 core, 8s pair and 5g opening. The paper displays every intervening cell, full composition and conservation arguments, Smithium’s six-field record and its positive oxidation-count sequence 2 through 8.

The exact electromagnetic ratio 503846395469/3676744786 lies strictly between 137 and 138. Quotient/remainder and positive order establish the unique One-ceiling endpoint and exclude every later positive charge. The complete coefficient derivation is included.

Six completed V3 entries are represented by native Lean 4 proofs, full candidate classifications, retained source-output checks and zero-axiom audit records. The original IUPAC comparison matches all seven noble closures through 118; g-block opening, Smithium and endpoint retain their standing-prediction status. Pinned original sources, native proof dependencies and exact reproduction code accompany the paper.
